_about: Tamako (151171, magatama_spirit): the magatama spirit, a little girl who talks like a doting old granny (婆 = "Granny", タマ婆 = "Granny Tama", 愛い子 = "dearie"). Translated from the game's Japanese. Global names/terms: Yakumo, Manoka, Murakumo, Suzuka, Shinobu, Stella, Alk, Yae, the Three Sacred Treasures, Yamata no Orochi, the Diviners' Commission, Spy (隠密, the Ninja of Yamato), Yamato, the Land of Wa. Own: Yasakani no Magatama (八坂瓊曲玉), Mafutsu no Kagami (真経津鏡), Light That Unravels the Night (skill, as in units.json).
profile: The incarnation of the spirit jewel, one of the Three Sacred Treasures. Long ago, she was swallowed by a curse along with her masters and became Yamata no Orochi. Freed from that curse, she ended up as everyone's cute Granny Tama. She's a dab hand at making ohagi, dearie.
titleCondition: Level Tamako to 100 and obtain her Amity Scroll

speech.home/oo_uikoyo: Oh, dearie, perfect timing. The ohagi's just finished. Won't you have some with me? Comes with hot tea right now~.
speech.home/murakumomomanokamo: Murakumo and Manoka have both softened up so much. If anything, they're getting a little giddy-- Hoho. Quite the heartbreaker, aren't I?
speech.home/ibunkakoryu: Cultural exchange is such fun~. Here, here, look. Yae and I tried filming a dance short. Is Granny cute? Do I look good?
speech.home/kanjotowa: Feelings are difficult things. They squeeze your heart even when you don't want them to... Say, dearie. When it gets hard to breathe, come sit by Granny. Granny will rub your back anytime.
speech.home/oya_kyono: Oh my. Are you feeling all muddled today? Then how about blowing off some steam with Granny? Scribble it all out, or go kaboom. Even something a teensy bit naughty is fine~.
speech.home/stellatoyakumowa: When I look at Stella and Yakumo, my heart just goes all tight~. Lately I figured out why. --Simply put, they give off strong grandchild energy...!
speech.ally/join: The spirit jewel Tamako, at your service-- Hoho. Pleased to meet you, dearie. Just call me Granny Tama. Now, how about some ohagi?
speech.ally/evolution: When your heart grows dark, come to Granny's side. You can cry, get angry, even hate. Granny will always listen and rub your back. I'm your Granny Tama, after all.

1.title: The Third Treasure
1.summary: Wandering the Land of Wa in search of the magatama, the last of the Three Sacred Treasures, Stella and the others meet Tamako, a spirit jewel who gained human form thanks to the village children. Freed from her curse by cheerful people, Tamako moves to Starview Village so the villagers won't be dragged into conflict.

lines.5: This is our masters' curse. They suffered, resented, and hated.
lines.6: And they wished. To be swallowed by the curse. For the ruin of all--
lines.10: You too will give birth to a curse, won't you?
lines.16: We are looking for a magatama.
lines.17: It is one of the Three Sacred Treasures. Have you seen it?
lines.20: Hmm. I dunno. What's a sacred treasure?
lines.22: A treasure with great power. Only the magatama has not been found yet.
lines.26: ...There are ninja trying to use that magatama to summon a dangerous yokai. We need to find it before they--
lines.31: Is Ms. Magatama not here either?
lines.35: ...Murakumo and Alk are asking around in the other villages too. If we can just find a lead...
lines.39: ...Do the spies still want to revive Orochi?
lines.43: ...I think fewer of them wish for that now. But they haven't completely disappeared.
lines.45: I don't sense any sinister presence right now, but if the magatama fell into their hands...
lines.48: My, my. What gloomy faces you have.
lines.52: If you like, won't you tell this old granny about it? It might cheer you up a teensy bit.
lines.67: Hoho, my. Found out already, am I~.
lines.73: --The spirit jewel Tamako, at your service.
lines.76: Hoho. The amulet magatama, Granny Tama. Just call me Granny Tama, dearie.
lines.79: Whoa! What was that!? Granny Tama, you're a sacred treasure!?
lines.81: I was called that once upon a time. Now I'm just everyone's Granny Tama~.
lines.89: Well, I'm sure there's a lot to catch up on. For now--
lines.99: It is delicious. Sweet and chewy.
lines.102: Hoho, what a fine appetite. Makes it worth cooking. Want some of this one too?
lines.107: It is delicious. Thank you for the food...!
lines.111: My, my, you've had a hard time of it. To think there was bad blood between the spies and the Diviners' Commission.
lines.113: Sorry for all the trouble, and thank you for looking for me~.
lines.121: Why I look like a bright young girl, you mean?
lines.124: Simple. The children of this village wished for Granny to be "like this".
lines.127: The child who picked Granny up was a good one. Kept Granny close as a simple charm. And the whole village is, well, so easygoing--
lines.136: Just watching that, well. My stiff old heart came completely unraveled~.
lines.139: Besides, the children love this form. A cute granny, isn't that nice?
lines.144: Have you forgotten the past? ...Our masters, who were killed?
lines.149: No. I remember, Mafutsu no Kagami. ...And that we became Orochi together without me ever doing anything for them.
lines.152: That's exactly why. Granny never wants to be swallowed by a curse again.
lines.155: And I don't want to see people swallowed by curses either. I want to spend my days slow and easy with humans.
lines.157: That's Granny's wish now. A teensy bit selfish, maybe.
lines.162: ...For the Diviners' Commission, it'd be best if you were with us. But if you want to stay in this village--
lines.167: ...Oh! No, no, I'm sorry. It's the other way around.
lines.169: Dearies. Won't you take Granny in?
lines.174: Oh, I won't forget to come home. This is Granny's hometown now.
lines.177: It wouldn't do for spies to come to this village and cause trouble. I'd be grateful if you'd look after me.
lines.180: Besides, you seem to have unraveled Mafutsu no Kagami's-- no, Manoka's curse. I'd like to thank you for that too.
lines.187: Hoho. I see, I see. Maybe you unraveled each other.
lines.190: ...But you still look troubled when it comes to the spies, don't you?
lines.193: Oh, I'm confident in the wisdom of age. I think I can at least help unravel your troubles.
lines.195: For instance, by making you all some ohagi?
lines.205: Yes. Welcome to Starview Village, Tamako.
lines.214: Alrighty. Here I go~. Hyper Granny Tama straight ball!
lines.217: It really is a good place. No wonder you two turned out the way you did. Murakumo, Manoka.
lines.221: She's become awfully human... More than us, wouldn't you say?
lines.225: Oh, you think so too, Murakumo? I was surprised as well.
lines.227: After all, she called it her own "wish". ...Are we not meant to grant the wishes of others?
lines.231: Hoho, that's true. Granny is still the same kind of being as you two.
lines.234: But Granny's Granny Tama now, you see? My way of living might be a teensy bit different from yours--
lines.236: I just want to unravel everyone's hearts. That's all.

2.title: Unraveling the Night
2.summary: Hearing Yakumo's worries about wanting to persuade a spy still plotting Orochi's revival, Tamako suggests going to the spy and cooking dinner. After a peaceful life free of curses, the spy pours out their pain, and Tamako saves their heart, laughing cheerfully even as she grieves for the people of the world.

lines.5: Say, absent-minded one. How about some dumplings and hot tea?
lines.9: ...Thank you. Did you make these yourself too?
lines.12: Yes, it's rather fun. If you want to make them with Manoka, I'll teach you the recipe.
lines.15: Now then, absent-minded one. Thinking about something you're keeping even from Manoka?
lines.19: ...It's about the spies targeting you all. That's exactly why it's not something to talk about...
lines.22: But you're no good at keeping secrets, are you? Especially from Manoka.
lines.27: Come now. Before Manoka finds out by accident, why not at least grumble to Granny~?
lines.32: ...I found one seed of rebellion. I've already disarmed them and reported it to the diviners.
lines.35: But that spy hasn't given up on reviving Orochi-- on revenge against the shogun and the Diviners' Commission.
lines.42: ...That's a tough one. Choosing such a dark path...
lines.46: ...I'd like to persuade them, so they don't run wild. But--
lines.50: ...When I asked the others from my village, all they said was "don't know" and "no idea"...
lines.53: ...They also said there are ways to break their spirit. But that's not the kind of method I want...
lines.59: Hoho, what colorful folks. Quite the fun bunch, aren't they?
lines.63: ...But I'm a deserter too. I really have no right to persuade them.
lines.66: I've cut people off before so I wouldn't be lumped in with them. ...Even though our hands are stained with the same blood.
lines.72: And still, Yakumo, you want to unravel that spy's suffering.
lines.76: Well then, why not leave this one to Granny?
lines.82: Your resentment won't fade, will it.
lines.85: You don't need to be bound anymore. You could even cast aside being a ninja and choose freedom.
lines.87: Even so, do you wish for revenge...? For a curse upon this world?
lines.90: I do. Revenge on those who denied us and cast us aside.
lines.92: Cursed magatama. Tool swallowed by Orochi. I'll give you this defiled body...! So please, grant my wish--!!
lines.99: One who births curses and wishes for curses. Then--
lines.102: First, may I make you some supper?
lines.110: Was this much enough? There's seconds too, so just say the word.
lines.113: ...Wh-why won't you grant my wish? I truly want revenge...
lines.115: Now, now, there's no poison in it. Won't you try a bite?
lines.118: My name is Tamako. My specialty is miso soup.
lines.120: Granny wants to know more about you. I'd be happy if you'd humor Granny's selfishness for a little while.
lines.123: ...E-even if you say that, I don't know what to do. I don't need anything like this...
lines.125: Oh my, is that so? Was the miso soup not good?
lines.131: By the way, do you have a favorite food? Granny's quite fond of pickled radish--
lines.142: I never cared about meals. Being a ninja was everything. And yet...
lines.145: ...It hurts, doesn't it. Being told you never needed to stain your hands with blood.
lines.147: Even though your pain, your resentment-- your regret-- can never be undone...
lines.153: I'm sorry I couldn't find you sooner.
lines.154: You've worked so hard all this time...
lines.157: It's all right to be defiled. Granny wants you to live.
lines.158: I'll hold your hand until you stop crying...
lines.161: It still hurts. The resentment won't fade. How... can I make this curse go away...?
lines.169: Oh, there's no need to rush. Let's unravel it slowly, with Granny.
lines.172: ...For now. Why don't we try making some ohagi together?
lines.179: ...You really saved us. But how on earth did you...
lines.182: Oh, we just made some tasty ohagi together, that's all.
lines.186: ...Don't you resent them? The ones who killed your masters?
lines.190: I'm not fond of them. But sadness might come first.
lines.193: In every age, people keep giving birth to curses. Truly, how pitiful...
lines.197: ...But you know how to unravel them.
lines.200: I want to learn that too. ...Thank you.
lines.204: Hoho. In your case, a time might come when you want to learn how to move a romance along too~?
lines.207: Oh, Granny will listen as many times as you like and rub your back.
lines.209: I'm everyone's Granny Tama, after all.

3.title: Unraveling Night After Night
3.summary: Saved from her curse by Tamako, the spy became a school teacher, but she is troubled by how different she is from Shinobu and Yakumo, ninja who should be just as defiled. Tamako listens to her worries and shows her ways to blow off steam, unraveling her troubles, and laughs cheerfully, cherishing such people.

lines.6: Haaah. Delicious. Cake is so nice...
lines.8: Granny might want to master the way of Western sweets like this...
lines.12: Will you not make ohagi anymore...?
lines.16: Stella. The very first thing I'll make is... ohagi cake...!
lines.19: ...Is it really okay for me to be here...?
lines.22: Hoho, of course. Today's a catch-up party, after all.
lines.23: You became a school teacher, didn't you? Are you having fun?
lines.26: ...There are several ninja hiding in Shibuya's schools. I've just become one of them.
lines.28: ...I have no intention of revenge anymore. I can truly feel that from the heart.
lines.29: I'm fine. ...You don't need to worry about me.
lines.31: I see, I see. That's wonderful.
lines.36: Oh, those are school uniforms. Your students?
lines.39: There's a ninja among them. He's completely blended in with the people of Shibuya.
lines.41: Even though we're both ninja. ...Far better than me.
lines.43: Hey, it's teach! Wanna get crêpes with us? Shinobu's actually interested for once--
lines.47: ...S-sorry. They talk to me a lot, and... I don't know how I should deal with them...
lines.50: Do you dislike the ninja who was with them?
lines.56: Take your time. Won't you tell me what you're thinking right now?
lines.59: ...Why... don't Shinobu and Yakumo carry any resentment? --When they're just as defiled.
lines.62: ...You don't intend to take revenge. But your own resentment won't fade?
lines.65: ...I'm sorry. Even though you unraveled my curse.
lines.66: It's just envy. Something ugly inside me. I shouldn't have feelings like this...
lines.69: No. That's something you're allowed to have.
lines.72: Feelings are born on their own, after all. Holding them down only makes it hard to breathe.
lines.74: Even Granny certainly doesn't love all of humanity~. If you dislike something, you dislike it, right?
lines.85: Oh, what a fine thing to say. Granny will start using that too.
lines.88: Still, what hurts, hurts. Sometimes food and sleep aren't enough to let it out...
lines.91: Well now. If ohagi isn't enough, why not try some other ways of blowing off steam?
lines.100: Stress relief method number one. --The doodle!
lines.103: Scribble it out, wham, bam, all messy. It's refreshing, and it's art too. Two birds with one stone...!
lines.106: Well, it's a bit like taking it out on something. Won't you push all that muddle onto the paper?
lines.109: Hoho. We're not done yet, you know? Next up--
lines.118: Here I go! --That stubborn, clueless, slave-driving boooooss!!!!!!
lines.121: Next... how about this "karaoke" thing. Yelling insults really loud...
lines.123: Ooh, that's refreshing~. It's a private room, so nobody else will hear.
lines.126: ...Is "pie throwing" not allowed? Apparently it's Shibuya culture. Pies, in the shoguns' faces...
lines.129: Hmmm. Tempting, but that's juuust over the line, I think~. Playing it among ourselves would be fine, though~.
lines.134: Yes, yes. It's a hard world~.
lines.140: Hey, Tamako. Something like this was all I needed...
lines.143: Well, I'm sure it depends on the person. But if it turned into a good day, that's wonderful.
lines.146: Did you have fun today, Stella?
lines.150: I thought insults and stabbing kunai were difficult.
lines.152: But fireworks and doodling were fun.
lines.156: I see, I see. Then that's all that matters~.
lines.159: ...Silly or serious, it's all right if it starts to hurt again.
lines.160: Granny will always be by your side.
lines.163: After all, there are children who'll throw themselves right into a curse. Isn't that so, Murakumo, Manoka?
lines.168: Hahaha. But this Murakumo is a sword. If my master wishes it, I can only cut, no?
lines.171: If a curse is one's true wish, is it not fine to grant it?
lines.179: Even Murakumo and the others are kids to you...?
lines.183: Hmm. If you say a desire to swing a sword around is childish-- I suppose I can't deny it.
lines.188: Hmmm. In the end, it's about the state of one's heart. Everyone's different, after all. And besides--
lines.191: Granny adores you all just the way you are. Honestly, what am I to do with you~.
